fact: One Citizen Daily reports the launch of the National Communication Authority e-Services Platform, on which licensing and payments that once required office visits can now be completed online.
The Ministry of Justice's Business Registration Service portal lets users apply online to validate a business, submit the application and receive approval notification.

The page says one eServices.gov.ss account, created with an ID for citizens and residents or a passport number for foreigners, gives access to all government services online including BRS, with fees payable by mobile money, cards and online banking.

The eServices portal offers online applications for permits and clearances from the revenue authorities, the Bureau of Standards accreditation permit, TIN registration on eTax and business registration, with payment online and permit delivered as PDF.

The portal describes a single username and password giving access to services of several agencies (revenue authorities, Bureau of Standards, business registration), as a single account for all government to citizen services.

A Republic Order from President Salva Kiir gave the E-Service Board full authority to digitise all government institutions by January 2026, with the board chair saying e-service rollout is under way across payments, licensing and records.
